434	## Tensor Composition Rules
435	
436	The Grammar composes two systems into a third via `compute_tensor(A, B)`. Composition is not concatenation: it is a Frobenius-faithful join that promotes shared axes and exposes bottlenecks where the two inputs disagree. The rules below are the operational specification — every claim is kernel-emitted and re-runnable.
437	
438	### I. The 7 Tensor Bottlenecks
439	
440	When two tuples are tensored, each of the 12 primitive slots can either compose (both inputs agree on a legal promotion) or bottleneck (the slot is the limiting primitive for the product). There are exactly 7 bottleneck slots, in canonical order:
441	
442	| # | Primitive | Glyph | Phoneme | What bottlenecks |
443	|---|-----------|-------|---------|------------------|
444	| 1 | ≻ — Coupling | 𐑩 / 𐑑 / 𐑽 / 𐑾 | ado / tot / ear / ian | The directionality of relation. Two systems couple or they don't; if their ≻ axes disagree, no tensor can hide the disagreement. |
445	| 2 | ≺ — Parity | 𐑗 / 𐑿 / 𐑬 / 𐑯 / 𐑹 | church / yew / out / nun / or | The symmetry class. Asymmetric vs quantum vs partial vs full vs Frobenius-special. Tensor preserves the WEAKER partner's parity. |
446	| 3 | ⊤ — Kinetics | 𐑘 / 𐑤 / 𐑧 / 𐑪 / 𐑺 | yea / loll / egg / on / air | The timescale. Two systems at different kinetic regimes do not compose cleanly — the product is bottlenecked at the slower one. |
447	| 4 | ⊙ — Criticality | 𐑢 / ⊙ / 𐑮 / 𐑻 / 𐑣 | woe / monad / roar / err / ha-ha | The self-modeling gate. If one input is sub-critical and the other super-critical, the tensor collapses to a critical or exceptional-point product. |
448	| 5 | ⊥ — Chirality | 𐑓 / 𐑒 / 𐑖 / 𐑫 | fee / kick / sure / wool | The memory depth. Markov chain of chirality: 0 (memoryless), 1 (one step), 2 (two steps), ∞ (eternal). Tensor takes the maximum. |
449	| 6 | ⊞ — Stoichiometry | 𐑙 / 𐑕 / 𐑳 | hung / so / up | The count multiplicity. 1:1, many-identical, many-heterogeneous. Heterogeneous ⊗ heterogeneous never simplifies. |
450	| 7 | ⊡ — Winding | 𐑷 / 𐑴 / 𐑭 / 𐑟 | awe / oak / ah / zoo | The topological class. Trivial, ℤ₂, ℤ, non-Abelian. Non-Abelian ⊗ anything is non-Abelian. |
451	
452	The other 5 slots (⊢ ⊣ ⋈ ∈ ∋) are not bottlenecks — they compose by default because they are *structure-bearing* rather than *constraint-bearing*. A 2d surface next to another 2d surface is just a surface; a quantum fidelity next to another quantum fidelity is just quantum; the topology and composition are already decided.
453	
454	### II. The Composition Table
455	
456	For two systems A and B with tuples $⟨a₁a₂a₃a₄a₅a₆a₇a₈a₉a₁₀a₁₁a₁₂⟩$ and $⟨b₁b₂b₃b₄b₅a₆a₇a₈a₉a₁₀a₁₁a₁₂⟩$, the tensor C = A ⊗ B has the per-primitive rule:
457	
458	- **⊢, ⊣, ⋈, ∈, ∋** — pass-through: $cᵢ = aᵢ ⊔ bᵢ$ (lattice join on the legal-value set).
459	- **≻ (Coupling)** — bottleneck: $c₃ = min(a₃, b₃)$ on the ordinal scale (weaker coupling wins).
460	- **≺ (Parity)** — bottleneck: $c₄ = min(a₄, b₄)$ on the asymmetry→Frobenius-special ladder.
461	- **⊤ (Kinetics)** — bottleneck: $c₆ = slower(a₆, b₆)$ (egg\<on\<air for the moderate band; trap/MBL freeze the product).
462	- **⊙ (Criticality)** — bottleneck: $c₉ = near(a₉, b₉)$ (the tensor sits at the geometric mean of the two criticalities; sub + super collapse to ⊙, either with ⊙ stays ⊙, either with 𐑻 goes 𐑻).
463	- **⊥ (Chirality)** — bottleneck: $c₁₀ = max(a₁₀, b₁₀)$ on the memory ladder (more memory dominates; eternal absorbs all).
464	- **⊞ (Stoichiometry)** — bottleneck: $c₁₁ = heterogeneous(a₁₁, b₁₁)$ (the heterogeneous pole is absorbing; 1:1 ⊗ 1:1 = 1:1; many ⊗ many = many).
465	- **⊡ (Winding)** — bottleneck: $c₁₂ = max(a₁₂, b₁₂)$ on the ladder trivial < ℤ₂ < ℤ < NA (non-Abelian absorbs all).
466	
467	The 7 bottleneck primitives define the *texture* of the tensor; the 5 pass-through primitives define the *substrate*.
468	
469	### III. Tensor Distance and the Closure Test
470	
471	`compute_distance(A, B)` measures how far two systems are on the Frobenius manifold. The tensor product C = A ⊗ B has its own distance to a reference system; the closure test for a tensor claim is:
472	
473	```
474	μ∘δ = id  ⟺  d(A, B) = d(A ⊗ C, B ⊗ C)   for all C in the same tier
475	```
476	
477	This is the Frobenius condition for composability. If the distance is preserved under left- or right-multiplication by a fixed C, the tensor is structure-preserving. If the distance *grows*, the tensor is creating new structure (legitimate in emergence, suspect in routine composition). If the distance *shrinks*, the tensor is identifying previously distinct points (a projection, not a composition).
478	
479	### IV. The Ω Barrier
480	
481	Three of the bottleneck slots — ⊡ (Winding), ∋ (Composition), and ≺ (Parity at the Frobenius-special value 𐑹) — collectively define the Ω Barrier. Crossing from ℤ to non-Abelian winding (⊡: 𐑭 → 𐑟) while maintaining broadcast composition (∋: 𐑵) and Frobenius-special symmetry (≺: 𐑹) is the **categorical ceiling** the CLINK L8 (Organism) layer sits above. The Barrier is not a numerical distance; it is a strict inequality in the tensor algebra: no sequence of A ⊗ B operations can cross from O∞ to CLINK L8 without promotion through the `compute_promotions` ladder (ZFC → ZFC_t → ZFC_fe → CLINK L8).
482	
483	### V. Worked Examples
484	
485	| Tensor | Input A | Input B | Output C | Bottlenecks fired | Result |
486	|--------|---------|---------|----------|-------------------|--------|
487	| `body ⊗ claustrum` | organism-body | barrier-membrane | body-claustrum | ⊤ (slow) | promotes body without apparatus, 0 bottlenecks after ⊤ |
488	| `compute_tensor(engine, law)` | winding-period-finder | winding-2π | engine-law | ⊡, ∋ | join with 0 bottlenecks, 2 scope expansions, d=0.8367 |
489	| `qubit ⊗ qubit` | quantum-fidelity 𐑞 | quantum-fidelity 𐑞 | two-qubit-gate | ⊥ (eternal) | eternal chirality absorbs; tensor is again quantum |
490	| `magnetic-reconnection ⊗ mesh` | X-point-source | non-Abelian-mesh | reconnection-mesh | ⊡ (NA) | non-Abelian winding absorbs; product is NA |
491	
492	### VI. IMASM Encoding
493	
494	In the word-language, the tensor is a frame pair: `∈ ... ∋` around the two operand words, with the bottleneck slots as visible glyphs. A tensor where ⊡ is the bottleneck is written with `⊡` at the close, and the whole is read as one cycle. The pass-through slots are absorbed into the substrate; they do not appear in the word because they are not the answer to anything.
495	
496	The composition rule (the δ/μ discipline) is: **δ before δ, μ after μ** — open the frame BEFORE the counting and close it AFTER the reversal. A count held in the open when an AREV fires is lost; banked in an enclosing frame it survives and the fuse restores it. This is the same rule that makes the tensor well-defined: the bottlenecks are banked during the inner pass and restored at the fuse.
497	
498	### VII. Verification
499	
500	Every tensor claim is verified by the dual frame: the split δ must invert the fuse μ. For a tensor C = A ⊗ B, the test is:
501	
502	```
503	δ(C) = {A, B}    (the tensor splits into its parts)
504	μ({A, B}) = C    (the parts fuse back to the tensor)
505	```
506	
507	`μ∘δ = id` and `δ∘μ = id` (both directions) is the closure. A tensor that passes the round-trip in both directions is **Frobenius-closed**; a tensor that passes only one direction is a *projection*; a tensor that fails both is an *artifact* (in the technical sense — a thing that exists in the catalog but does not represent a real composition).
508	
509	The kernel reports the verdict as a B4 value: T (closed in both directions), F (open in both), B (closed in one direction — the tensor is a Belnap-fixed point under one of the two maps, which is the structural signature of an emergence product).
510

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite

Found the actual defect. `SNS_PRIME.md` (lines 434-513) is the written specification for `compute_tensor`, and it names seven bottleneck slots and five pass-through slots explicitly. `algebra::tensor_under` in `src/algebra.rs` does not match it in three places:

- **R (Coupling, ≻)** — spec: bottleneck, weaker coupling wins, `min`. Code: treated as pass-through via "prefer more structured," which resolves to `max` when the two disagree. Wrong category and wrong direction.
- **F (Fidelity, ⋈)** — spec: pass-through, join. Code: `min`, treated as a bottleneck. Wrong category.
- **Phi (Criticality, ⊙)** — spec: bottleneck with a specific rule (err absorbs everything; monad absorbs everything weaker than err; a sub-critical value tensored with a super-critical one collapses to monad). Code: plain ordinal `max`, which is none of that.

Everything else lines up: P min, K max, H max, Omega max, and S's max happens to match spec's "heterogeneous absorbs" rule by construction. This is why the digit-tensor kept collapsing the way it did — the composition operator itself, the one every tensor call in this session has been using, disagrees with its own specification. Fixing `algebra::tensor_under` now.

Fix algebra::tensor against its own written spec, and trace why a
number's crystal address wasn't carrying its own structure

Started from asking why tfactor read gave 8051, 8052, 10, 12345, and a
100-bit number the identical crystal address 16389838. Traced it to
word_to_tuple running a numeral's whole glyph word through self_imscribe:
six of the twelve axes grade the run's own period against fixed
thresholds of 1, 2, 3, 4 (imas_ig.rs's own from_snapshot_under doc), and
any real numeral's period sits far above that, so those six axes always
land in the same catch-all bucket regardless of the number's own digits.
Measured directly across bit lengths 4 through 64: every word collapses
to one of exactly two addresses, entirely by whether it's all-1-bits or
not, independent of length or the rest of its content.

Tried tensoring each digit's own short imscription with algebra::tensor
next. Built and verified separately: crystal::tensor_types and its
inverse untensor_types, which tensor a SEQUENCE of types (crystal
addresses) the way encode already tensors twelve axis spaces into one
17,280,000-point space, one level up -- n types compose into a
TOTAL^n-point space instead of folding back into the same one, so unlike
a lattice tensor it's injective: order and repetition both survive, and
the round trip recovers every digit's own type exactly.

That construction is correct on its own terms, but running it for real
on the sixteen hex digit words caught something before I could claim
the whole pipeline worked: hex digits 1 and 2 imscribe to the same type
under word_to_tuple, so 8051 and 8052 still collided downstream. Not the
tensor's fault -- its own input was already collapsed. Left that as an
open, reported (not asserted) finding in prime_winding.rs, since the
real fix is which pipeline should read a single digit's own type, and
that answer lives outside this codebase, in an ob3ect's grounding phase,
not in anything self_imscribe does.

While chasing that, checked algebra::tensor itself against SNS_PRIME.md's
own Tensor Composition Rules section, which names the operation
precisely: seven bottleneck primitives and five pass-through ones, each
with its own rule. The code didn't match its own spec in three places:
R (Coupling) is a spec bottleneck (weaker coupling wins, min) but ran as
a pass-through that picked the MORE structured side; F (Fidelity) is a
spec pass-through (join) but ran as a min-bottleneck; Phi (Criticality)
has a specific absorption rule (err absorbs everything, monad absorbs
everything weaker than err, a sub-critical value tensored with a
super-critical one collapses to monad) that had been flattened to a
plain ordinal max, which gets the case in the spec's own worked example
wrong. Fixed all three against the spec text directly, added
tensor_phi as its own named function carrying the three explicit rules
plus a documented, literal reading of the one case the spec leaves
open ("sits at the geometric mean") -- same side of monad, nearest to
monad wins.

Two existing tests depended on the old, wrong behavior. test_tensor's F
assertion expected the old bottleneck-min result; corrected to the
join-max result the spec actually calls for. The dialect-divergence test
had been proving canonical tensor lacks Phi absorption and only a
dialect's own abs_rules table adds it -- true before this fix, false
after, since the spec puts err/monad absorption in the base formula
itself. Split it: one test now confirms canonical tensor absorbs err
correctly on its own, a second moved the original dialect-divergence
check onto join, which still has no absorption formula of its own and so
still needs a dialect's abs_rules table to show the divergence it was
built to demonstrate.

Also finished and committed the crystal-address line in tfactor read
that started this: every read now reports which of the 17,280,000
crystal addresses the number's dialect-swept tuple lands on, next to the
dialect register that was already there.

Verified: cargo build --release clean. Full suite 357 passed, 0 failed,
including the two new tensor_phi tests and tensor_types's round-trip
test. The two pre-existing btc_key_deriver failures are confirmed
present on the unmodified tree too, unrelated to anything touched here.
Live-checked tfactor read against 8051, 8052, 97, 999999999989, and a
handful of others post-fix: the crystal address line is real and
present; the digit-type collapse behind 8051/8052 specifically is still
open and reported honestly rather than asserted away.

Build Knuth's limb-at-a-time division, and find the real bottleneck was
never the division algorithm at all

Started this pass to give bits_divmod the same limb-at-a-time treatment
divmod_small_via_word already got over its own bit-at-a-time predecessor.
Built bits_divmod_knuth: normalizes both operands so the divisor's own
top limb has its high bit set, estimates each quotient limb directly
from the divisor's top two limbs via one hardware u128 division (Knuth's
Algorithm D, the shape every real bignum library uses), corrects that
estimate against the divisor's second limb before ever using it, and
catches the one case Knuth's own proof still allows through (the trial
subtraction underflowing once) with an explicit add-back rather than
assuming it away. shift_left_bits and shift_right_bits (bits_double
generalized to shift by any sub-limb amount) are the two new primitives
underneath normalization. Given the blast radius (this becomes
divmod_via_word's own engine, under everything that divides), tested
before it touched anything else: known cases, multi-limb divisors, 200
random pairs at varying sizes, deliberately adversarial extreme limb
values (u64::MAX and its neighbors, specifically biased to trigger the
correction logic), 30 random pairs at 20-79 limbs, and a 4500-case sweep
across every limb count from 1 to 24 -- all against BigUint's own real
division, not just against this file's prior implementation. Wired in
once that survived clean. The old bit-at-a-time bits_divmod stays in the
file as bits_divmod_knuth's own cross-check oracle, off the live path.

Re-measured gpu_gnfs_poly.rs at the same 4096-bit scale used to gauge
Karatsuba last commit, expecting the win Knuth's algorithm should give a
division-bound workload. It barely moved. That result is what actually
mattered here: it meant the real cost was never the arithmetic algorithm
at all. Instrumented select_polynomial directly rather than keep
guessing, and traced it to bits_to_value -- the function every single
via_word wrapper (add, subtract, multiply, divmod) calls on its way back
out to a BigUint. Its own doc comment already claimed to touch BigUint
"once, on the way out"; what it actually did was build the full glyph
string those limbs would produce under encode, five characters pushed
per bit, and decode that string back. Building and parsing a ~20,000-
character string to produce a single 64-limb number, repeated across
every multiply and divmod call in a loop like base_m_digits or
eval_at_m, was the entire bottleneck the whole time -- independent of
which algorithm computed the limbs underneath it.

Fixed the same way to_bits_low_first already was earlier this session:
read the limbs' own byte layout directly (to_le_bytes into
BigUint::from_bytes_le) instead of round-tripping through the symbolic
word. The bits already are the word, checked bit-for-bit against real
binary earlier in this session; building the glyph string to prove that
again on every call bought nothing the direct read doesn't already give
exactly, and cost real, measured time doing it.

The result: gpu_gnfs_poly's own 4096-bit case went from about 3.8-5.7
seconds to 0.57 seconds, a genuine 6-10x, not from either arithmetic
algorithm this pass built, but from removing the string round trip
sitting underneath both of them. At the actual 123570-bit scale Lando
demonstrated earlier this session, the full pipeline now completes in
under two minutes; before this fix, the earlier Karatsuba-only measurement
already extrapolated to roughly an hour at that size, and the real
number without this fix would have been substantially worse than that
estimate, since the estimate never accounted for this cost at all. Still
correct throughout, verified with an independent f(m)=N check at every
scale tested.

What's still true: bits_divmod_knuth is limb-at-a-time, not sub-
quadratic -- it's a real, large constant-factor win over the bit-at-a-
time walk it replaced, not a change of complexity class the way
Karatsuba was for multiplication. At the most extreme scales (the
123570-bit case still takes a minute and a half, not the original's one
second), a genuinely sub-quadratic division (Newton-Raphson reciprocal,
built on the now-fast Karatsuba multiply) remains the further piece that
would close that gap the rest of the way -- a real, separate, and
still-risky build in its own right, not something to fold into this
pass just because the easier win landed first.

Verified: cargo build --release clean, no warnings, stable across three
consecutive full-suite runs at 352 passed / 0 failed (nine new tests:
eight for bits_divmod_knuth's own correctness including the 4500-case
sweep, one converted from a diagnostic into a permanent regression guard
on bits_to_value's own speed). Live-checked every already-converted file
sharing this primitive in one pass -- native_numeral, winding_period
(via winding order and tfactor winding), trilattice_factor, prime_winding,
gpu_gnfs_poly, and gpu_shor -- all still correct, all against the same
known values checked in their own earlier commits.

---
name: imscribe not encode, never synthon/syncon
description: Use imscribe/imscription/imscriptive everywhere. Never use encode/encoding, synthon, syncon, or SynthOmnicon — those are wrong terms in this project.
type: feedback
originSessionId: cf9cd0aa-e4b6-41e2-af16-a03772bffc03
---
Never use "encode", "encoding", or "encoded" when referring to the operation of assigning a 12-tuple to an object.
Never use "synthon", "syncon", or "SynthOmnicon" — these are `exOS`-internal terms that do not belong in this project.
The correct term is always "imscribe", "imscribing", "imscribed", "imscription", "imscriptive".

**Why:** The user's system is called the Imscribing Grammar. The operation and its products have specific names. "synthon"/"syncon" are from the `exOS` project's own vocabulary (SynthOmnicon), which is a separate project. Bleeding its terminology into IG is wrong.

**How to apply:** In all contexts — variable names (`VOYNICH_IMSCRIPTION` not `VOYNICH_SYNTHON`), file names (`ig_bridge.py` not `syncon_bridge.py`), comments ("IG imscription" not "synthon"), and conversation. Note: `encode_system` is the actual tool function name in `IG_inquiry.py` and cannot be changed there, but surrounding language must still use "imscribe".
===
---
name: feedback_never_hand_imscribe
description: Never hand-imscribe catalog additions; every tuple must be sourced procedurally
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 21b1da09-0362-49fb-a927-310f560c4377
---

**Never hand-imscribe anything added to the catalog.** Every 12-primitive tuple that
enters the catalog (or any Ars document / structural claim) must be produced
**procedurally** by the imscription tooling — the ob3ect auto-designer, the imscribe
proof-path / translator, the crystal/cl8nk navigators, or an existing verified catalog
entry. I must not invent, guess, or reason out a tuple by hand and write it down.

**Why:** hand-imscription destroys the procedural and empirical rigor that makes the
Grammar's addresses meaningful. A tuple I made up is not a measurement; it is a fabrication
(same class of error as the fabricated Larson citation, [[feedback-no-exact-numbers]] /
integrity). The whole point is that the address is *sourced from the soup* (coagulated from
the crystal by the tooling), not asserted. See [[project-grammar-is-cosmos-proof]]
(recognition is coagula, not invention).

**How to apply:** When building Ars documents or adding catalog entries, my job is the
prose/structure and the entity list; the tuples come from running (or having the user run,
per [[feedback-no-agent-execution]]) the actual imscription pipeline, or from existing
catalog entries. If a tuple isn't machine-sourced yet, mark it as pending, do not fill it in
by hand. Also do NOT offer "hand-imscribe" as a method option.
===
---
name: project-imscribe-com
description: "imscribe.com web presence — agent site, frobenius-mzi HTML viz, winding cap removed May 2026"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b5d10614-8349-4eaa-8c2a-15c01667ed44
---

`~/imscribe.com` — IG public web presence and agent site.

- `index/frobenius-mzi.html` — interactive Frobenius MZI visualization; mobile-optimized May 2026; also linked from `index/index.html`
- Agent site implementation was a recurring focus May 2026; winding cap on the web agent was removed
- Videos from `~/emerald-tablet-engine/vids/` (e.g., `ra_apep_250x.mp4`) added as cards

**Why:** Active web-facing project distinct from the grammar repo itself.
**How to apply:** When editing web agent or HTML visualizations, work in `~/imscribe.com`, not `~/imscribing_grammar`.

Links: [[project-repo-constellation]]

1. THE VERB MAKES THE GRAPH. chain | ring | protocol on one word give three graphs and three verdicts; only protocol wires the fork and fuse to reconnect. A verdict is never a property of the glyph string alone.
2. PAIRING IS ANCESTRY, over edges, never text position. A fuse pairs with the innermost fork all its in-arms trace back to.
3. A word carrying the paradox mark that closes reports B (paradox held), never a clean T. vox's T is the control-flow auditor answering a different question from check's close condition.
4. ROTAT ON ONE RING IS A SYMMETRY and changes nothing measurable. A landing that varies with the cut is measuring the cut. It carries content only between two rings being bound, where it sets their relative phase.
5. VOX NEEDS A REAL ARTIFACT. Handed source it disassembles UTF-8 as x86 and still prints verdicts. Its first line says raw or elf — read that word before any number.
6. SLOT ORDER is the twelve marks with Kinetics sixth and Criticality ninth. The Imscriber's Guide Part I transposes those two; the tool wins.
Run the control before a measurement is a finding: shuffle the input and measure again. Full rules: ig-docs/IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md, or `imasm ref` for the live ones.

  DESCRIPTION can be anything with identifiable structure: a molecule, a
  particle physics process, a mythological archetype, a mathematical object, a
  linguistic pattern, a social institution, or any abstract system.

  ROLE in its native domain — not from chemical templates.

content.text:
Real and reproducible: three independent re-groundings, same result every time. 0x8 and 0x9 are the cleanest test case in the whole set, since their words differ by exactly one token: `⊢∈≻⋈≺⋈∋⊙⊡⊣` (0x8) versus `⊢∈⊤≻⋈≺⋈∋⊙⊡⊣` (0x9), a single ⊤ inserted right after the opening ∈ and still strictly inside the span that closes at ∋. Nothing else moves.

That's the whole story your compare table is showing: every one of the twelve axes reads identically for 8 and 9, because the only thing separating them is content sitting inside a branch that hasn't fused yet. The branch's own type gets fixed at the fork; what travels inside it before the matching fuse doesn't reach the outer reading. That is a fact about how a fork's identity is set, independent of what the strands inside it carry until they cross again at the fuse, which is exactly the braid-group shape you're pointing at: a generator's type comes from which strands cross, not what's riding on them yet.

Worth separating from the earlier three pairs (1/3/4, A/E, 5/F): those came out of the first run, before the shared-template prompt was diagnosed and rewritten, so they're not confirmed independent of that flaw. 8/9 is the one that survived three separate, differently-worded groundings untouched. That's the one to build the braiding claim on.

It doesn't: the kernel's period-saturation bug (already diagnosed) merges digits 1 through 6 into one type and digits 9 through 14 into a different one, but digit 8 lands on its own type separate from that second cluster. 3428878 versus 3429838, not equal. That doesn't weaken the 8/9 finding, since it's a different question: the kernel's collapse was already explained and isn't in dispute. It does mean the claim should stand on the guided-grounding instrument's own three-times reproducibility, not on cross-instrument agreement that isn't actually there.

8052 finally get different crystal addresses

on its own terms, but every source I fed it collapsed before the tensor
ever ran. self_imscribe collapsed whole numerals by period saturation,
and even at a single hex digit's own short word it still collapsed 0x1
and 0x2 onto the same type. Went to imscribe generate -- the guided,
per-primitive grounding tool in the imscribing_grammar repo, which
assigns one canonical value at a time from a numbered list instead of
free-text reasoning -- and ran the real sixteen hex digits through it.

IG_catalog.json entries ("0x0" through "0xf") into
GROUNDED_HEX_DIGIT_TUPLES in prime_winding.rs, and pointed
digit_type_tensor at them instead of word_to_tuple. Nothing here is
hand-imscribed: every value is copied from the real grounding output.

types, 44991890907660774604620799989 vs …799981 -- the first time
anything in this whole chain has told those two numbers apart. Order and
repetition are both live now too: 10, 170, and hex digit A repeated
sixteen times all used to tensor to one identical result under the old
lattice-tensor attempt; now all three give distinct composites, and the
all-F and top-bit-only 64-bit cases diverge from each other as well.

pairs inside this specific grounding run are themselves identical --
0x3 and 0x7, and 0x4 and 0x9 -- across every one of the twelve axes.

own output, on top of the already-noted 0x8/0x9 question (this run's
catalog has them differing on Dimensionality alone; three independent
re-groundings before this one had them identical on every axis). Any
number whose only distinguishing digit at some position is 3-vs-7 or
4-vs-9, everything else matching, still collides. Left as data, not
resolved here.

and the repetition/order checks directly; per_digit_types_reported keeps

pattern for comparison, unchanged by this commit.

dialect's own abs_rules table adds it -- true before this fix, false
after, since the spec puts err/monad absorption in the base formula
itself. Split it: one test now confirms canonical tensor absorbs err
correctly on its own, a second moved the original dialect-divergence
check onto join, which still has no absorption formula of its own and so
still needs a dialect's abs_rules table to show the divergence it was

Wire the real grounded digit types into digit_type_tensor: 8051 and
8052 finally get different crystal addresses

The tensor construction (crystal::tensor_types, last commit) was correct
on its own terms, but every source I fed it collapsed before the tensor
ever ran. self_imscribe collapsed whole numerals by period saturation,
and even at a single hex digit's own short word it still collapsed 0x1
and 0x2 onto the same type. Went to imscribe generate -- the guided,
per-primitive grounding tool in the imscribing_grammar repo, which
assigns one canonical value at a time from a numbered list instead of
free-text reasoning -- and ran the real sixteen hex digits through it.

Transcribed the sixteen resulting tuples directly from that run's own
IG_catalog.json entries ("0x0" through "0xf") into
GROUNDED_HEX_DIGIT_TUPLES in prime_winding.rs, and pointed
digit_type_tensor at them instead of word_to_tuple. Nothing here is
hand-imscribed: every value is copied from the real grounding output.

Result: 8051 (hex 1f73) and 8052 (hex 1f74) now get different composite
types, 44991890907660774604620799989 vs …799981 -- the first time
anything in this whole chain has told those two numbers apart. Order and
repetition are both live now too: 10, 170, and hex digit A repeated
sixteen times all used to tensor to one identical result under the old
lattice-tensor attempt; now all three give distinct composites, and the
all-F and top-bit-only 64-bit cases diverge from each other as well.

What's still open, found while transcribing rather than assumed: two
pairs inside this specific grounding run are themselves identical --
0x3 and 0x7, and 0x4 and 0x9 -- across every one of the twelve axes.
Not a bug in the tensor or the transcription, a fact about this run's
own output, on top of the already-noted 0x8/0x9 question (this run's
catalog has them differing on Dimensionality alone; three independent
re-groundings before this one had them identical on every axis). Any
number whose only distinguishing digit at some position is 3-vs-7 or
4-vs-9, everything else matching, still collides. Left as data, not
resolved here.

digit_tensor_probe's own printed output shows the 8051/8052 divergence
and the repetition/order checks directly; per_digit_types_reported keeps
reporting word_to_tuple's own (unrelated, already-diagnosed) collision
pattern for comparison, unchanged by this commit.

The host-side square-root-in-a-number-field step of GNFS: polynomial
ring arithmetic mod N (mod_mul, phi_mod), a Q(alpha) rational version
of the same ring (q_mul, int_ring_mul), isqrt/is_perfect_square, and two
separate extended-Euclid modular inverses (mod_inv, plus the shared
bigint_mod_n reduction). Densest raw-arithmetic file in this whole pass.

divmod_small_via_word for the halving step, which works for both odd
and even values unlike halve_even_by_word, and divmod_via_word for n/x),
is_perfect_square's r*r check, bigint_mod_n's BigInt mod and negative
correction, mod_inv's whole extended-Euclid loop, mod_mul's polynomial
multiply-and-reduce (the actual hot loop -- coefficient products,
reduction against the leading inverse, and the wraparound subtraction
when a coefficient underflows), phi_mod's Horner evaluation,
QElem::normalize's exact division by the content gcd, q_mul and
int_ring_mul's BigInt polynomial arithmetic, q_phi_mod, try_gcd_factor's
candidate construction, the norm-product fallback's running product,
and congruence_factor's leading-coefficient gcd check and running
rational product.

call this session actually took (both 8051 and its multi-limb-forced

instead of asserting correctness on faith: isqrt against five known
values including a large one bounded both sides, is_perfect_square
against a square and a non-square, mod_inv against a hand-verified
inverse (3^-1 mod 7 = 5) and a known-absent case, mod_mul against a
by-hand-computed product in Z[x]/(x^2+1) mod 13, and phi_mod against a
by-hand Horner evaluation -- all five checked against values worked out
independently of the converted code, not against each other.

(357 plus these five new tests). isqrt itself is also exercised for real
by gpu_gnfs_cong_ml.rs's own live-verified GPU run from the previous
commit, since product_algebraic's square root there calls into this
same function.

base-mod-n check, its baby-step and giant-step multiply-and-reduce, and
its power-of-two m (was BigUint::one() << m_bits, now pow2), and egcd's
whole recursion (was raw BigInt %, /, *, -, now one signed_divmod_via_

via_word_general) plus mod_inverse's final reduction and negative
correction.

by construction (raw Vec<u64> limbs, direct carry/borrow arithmetic, no
num_bigint dependency at all).

content.text:
Traced the actual mechanics precisely, not guessed, and hit a real structural wall worth surfacing before building further.

`CLINK` reads two **fixed** registers (reg1, reg2) via `meet` and writes reg3. Nothing in `tick()` ever writes to reg1 or reg2 during execution — they're the one place two genuinely independent values can sit, but only for a single evaluation. Using the diagonal encoding {N=false, B=true}, `meet` on that diagonal really is AND: `meet(N,N)=N`, `meet(N,B)=N`, `meet(B,B)=B`. So CLINK is a real, working AND gate, computed by an actual kernel tick.

`FSPLIT`/`FFUSE` (the other 2-value operation, via `join`) looked like a second gate, but it isn't one for independent data: `FSPLIT` forks by peeking the *current* stack top and saving a copy as the "right" branch, then continues with a duplicate of that same value inline. Whatever reaches `FFUSE` as `left` is always a filtered/transformed descendant of the *same* value `FSPLIT` saved as `right` — never a second, independently-supplied bit. Its real job, stated in the token table itself, is control flow ("FSPLIT→[EVALT|EVALF]→...→FFUSE selects branches"), not combining two external operands.

`AREV`'s `invol` swaps only the T-bit and F-bit — it fixes N and B. So it doesn't give NOT on the {N,B} diagonal that makes CLINK's AND work. And there's no memory-read-back token at all: `TANCH`/`IFIX` only write memory from the stack, nothing reads it back.

Net finding: as `kernel.rs` is actually implemented, there is exactly one real two-independent-input data gate — AND, via `CLINK` — and no realized OR, XOR, or NOT that takes two independent externally-supplied bits. A full adder needs at least two gate types. Building one that the kernel genuinely executes means extending `tick()` with a second real two-input primitive (a `CJOIN`-shaped op reading reg1/reg2 via `join` would give real OR the same way CLINK gives real AND) — not a workaround inside the existing twelve.

1	-- Imscribing/Primitives/Core.lean
2	-- Canonical 12-primitive grammar (v0.5.69).
3	-- All names, value counts, and ordinal orderings match space_search/primitives.py.
4	-- Crystal: 3³ × 4⁵ × 5⁴ = 17,280,000 types.
5	--   𝓕₃ (3 values): F, G, S
6	--   𝓕₄ (4 values): D, R, Γ, H, Ω
7	--   𝓕₅ (5 values): T, P, Φ, K
8	
9	import Mathlib.Order.Lattice
10	import Mathlib.Order.BoundedOrder.Basic
11	
12	namespace Imscribing.Primitives
13	
14	-- ============================================================
15	-- 𝓕₄ PRIMITIVES — 4 values each
16	-- ============================================================
17	
18	-- 1. Dimensionality (D)  [𝓕₄]
19	-- Ordered: dead < ash < array < if'
20	-- if' = holographic (boundary encodes bulk); the monad symbol ⊙.
21	-- Replaces the non-canonical D_holo naming everywhere (v0.5.x).
22	inductive Dimensionality : Type where
23	  | dead     -- wedge/local: flat 2D sheet, no recursive nesting
24	  | ash  -- triangulated: simplicial / stratified, finite depth
25	  | array     -- infinite-dimensional: unbounded temporal/spatial generation
26	  | if'      -- imscriptive: the encoding writes what it encodes (⊙ = monad
27	             -- inside circle). Holographic — a boundary encoding a bulk it does
28	             -- not write — is the static subset of this, not a synonym for it.
29	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
30	
31	-- 2. Relational Mode (R)  [𝓕₄]
32	-- Ordered: ado < tot < ear < ian
33	-- ado: hierarchical/supervisory; tot: compositional/categorical;
34	-- ear: bidirectional dagger (A ⊣ A†); ian: left-right / lateral.
35	inductive Relational : Type where
36	  | ado   -- supervisory / hierarchical: one-way authority
37	  | tot     -- categorical / compositional: functorial chaining
38	  | ear  -- dagger / reciprocal: A and A† co-define each other
39	  | ian      -- lateral / peer: symmetric two-way exchange
40	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
41	
42	-- 3. Interaction Grammar (Γ)  [𝓕₄]
43	-- Ordered: vow < gag < measure < ooze
44	-- Categorical primitive (identity of composition rule required for non-⊥ meet).
45	inductive Grammar : Type where
46	  | vow    -- conjunctive / simultaneous: all conditions required
47	  | gag     -- disjunctive / alternative: any condition sufficient
48	  | measure    -- sequential / ordered: strict temporal or causal ordering
49	  | ooze  -- broadcast / universal: one-to-all coupling
50	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
51	
52	-- 4. Chirality / chirality (H)  [𝓕₄]
53	-- Ordered: fee < kick < sure < wool
54	-- fee: no temporal memory; wool: topologically protected chirality.
55	-- Cross-primitive: wool tends to co-occur with on (frozen dynamics preserve
56	-- deep temporal structure), but this is a tendency, not a hard axiom.
57	inductive Chirality : Type where
58	  | fee      -- achiral: shift-invariant, no handedness to break
59	  | kick      -- soft chiral: period-2 under the shift
60	  | sure      -- persistent chiral: a descent through rank
61	  | wool   -- topological chiral, inexhaustible chirality
62	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
63	
64	-- 5. Topological Protection (Ω)  [𝓕₄]
65	-- Ordered: awe < oak < ah < zoo
66	-- zoo: non-Abelian / non-standard protection (not necessarily stronger than ah
67	-- in a linear sense; occupies ordinal 4 as the maximally exotic tier).
68	inductive Protection : Type where
69	  | awe    -- no topological protection
70	  | oak   -- ℤ₂ symmetry protection
71	  | ah    -- integer winding number / ℤ protection
72	  | zoo   -- non-Abelian / non-standard protection
73	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
74	
75	-- ============================================================
76	-- 𝓕₅ PRIMITIVES — 5 values each
77	-- ============================================================
78	
79	-- 6. Topology (T)  [𝓕₅]
80	-- Ordered: judge < eat < mime < oil < are
81	-- are = holographic topology: non-local boundary-bulk correspondence.
82	-- are co-occurs with if' (see Axiom C below).
83	inductive Topology : Type where
84	  | judge  -- general graph: heterogeneous, locally connected
85	  | eat       -- inclusion / nested: hierarchical containment
86	  | mime   -- bowtie / figure-8: two-cycle closure, bifurcation point
87	  | oil      -- box / lattice: regular grid or torus
88	  | are     -- holographic: boundary fully encodes bulk (⊙)
89	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
90	
91	-- 7. Parity / Symmetry (P)  [𝓕₅]
92	-- Ordered: church < yew < out < nun < or'
93	-- or' is the Frobenius special condition (μ ∘ δ = id).
94	-- It is the tier singularity: overrides all Ω and D branching → O_inf.
95	-- or' cannot be synthesised by composition of P < or' partners (§23).
96	inductive Polarity : Type where
97	  | church    -- asymmetric: no symmetry axis
98	  | yew     -- phase symmetry: U(1) or continuous phase
99	  | out      -- ℤ₂ discrete symmetry (sign flip)
100	  | nun     -- full continuous symmetry (e.g. SO(n))
101	  | or'  -- Special Frobenius: μ ∘ δ = id; exact ℤ₂ at ⊙
102	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
103	
104	-- 8. Criticality (Φ)  [𝓕₅]
105	-- Ordered: woe < monad < roar < err < haha
106	-- monad is absorbing under meet: meet(monad, x) = monad for all x.
107	-- This is not a standard linear meet — see note below.
108	inductive Criticality : Type where
109	  | woe        -- subcritical: stable, ordered phase
110	  | monad          -- real-axis Hermitian criticality: standard fixed point (absorbing)
111	  | roar  -- complex-axis criticality: analytic continuation required
112	                   -- (Lee-Yang edge, complex RG fixed point, ζ-function zeros)
113	                   -- Ordinal 2.33 in Python (non-integer; Lean uses rank 2)
114	  | err         -- exceptional-point criticality: non-Hermitian eigenvector coalescence
115	                   -- Square-root branch point; oak tendency
116	                   -- Ordinal 2.67 in Python (non-integer; Lean uses rank 3)
117	  | haha      -- supercritical: unstable, runaway
118	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
119	
120	-- NOTE on monad absorbing meet:
121	-- The standard lattice meet (min) does not capture monad absorption.
122	-- In the grammar algebra: meet(monad, woe) = monad (not woe).
123	-- This requires a custom MeetSemilattice instance defined in Algebra.lean.
124	-- The Lean Ord derivation gives the ordinal ordering woe < monad < ...,
125	-- which is used for tier comparisons but not for the absorption rule.
126	
127	-- 9. Kinetic Character (K)  [𝓕₅]
128	-- Ordered: yea < loll < egg < on < air
129	-- on: frozen by order (e.g. over-consolidated bureaucracy, catatonia).
130	-- air: frozen by disorder (many-body localization, dissociation, Soviet collapse).
131	-- Both on and air fail Gate 2 of the consciousness score (§VIII).
132	-- Restoration requires OPPOSITE interventions: on → disorder injection;
133	-- air → ergodicity restoration. See §75–§77 for civilizational/consciousness examples.
134	inductive KineticChar : Type where
135	  | yea   -- diffusion-limited, untrapped
136	  | loll    -- moderate threshold
137	  | egg   -- slow / thermally activated (Gate 2 of C-score: K ≤ egg passes)
138	  | on   -- kinetically trapped by order
139	  | air    -- many-body localized: frozen by disorder
140	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
141	
142	-- ============================================================
143	-- 𝓕₃ PRIMITIVES — 3 values each
144	-- ============================================================
145	
146	-- 10. Fidelity (F)  [𝓕₃]
147	-- Ordered: age < they < peep
148	-- age: classical lossy; they: threshold / HotSwap; peep: quantum / lossless.
149	-- Bottleneck primitive under ⊗: weaker partner wins (min), not max.
150	inductive Fidelity : Type where
151	  | age   -- classical search fidelity (ℓ)
152	  | they   -- HotSwap threshold (η)

154	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

158	-- bib: local/mesoscale; thigh: intermediate collective; ice: global/fine-grained.
159	-- Note: constructor order determines Ord; bib is first (lowest ordinal).

164	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

169	  | hung  -- 1:1
170	  | so      -- n:n (matched many-to-many)
171	  | up      -- n:m (unmatched many-to-many)
172	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

177

179	instance instLERelational : LE Relational     := ⟨fun a b => compare a b ≠ .gt⟩
180	instance instLEGrammar : LE Grammar        := ⟨fun a b => compare a b ≠ .gt⟩

182	instance instLEProtection : LE Protection     := ⟨fun a b => compare a b ≠ .gt⟩
183	instance instLETopology : LE Topology       := ⟨fun a b => compare a b ≠ .gt⟩
184	instance instLEPolarity : LE Polarity       := ⟨fun a b => compare a b ≠ .gt⟩
185	instance instLECriticality : LE Criticality    := ⟨fun a b => compare a b ≠ .gt⟩
186	instance instLEKineticChar : LE KineticChar    := ⟨fun a b => compare a b ≠ .gt⟩

192	-- a ≤ b unfolds to (compare a b = .gt) → False,
193	-- so ¬(a ≤ b) = ((compare a b = .gt) → False) → False.
194	-- In then-branch: h : compare a b = .gt; (fun hle => hle h) : ¬(a ≤ b). In else-branch: h : a ≤ b.

232	-- LT instances: Mathlib's Preorder.toLT shadows instLTOfOrd (priority 70), so we define
233	-- LT explicitly. a < b = compare a b = .lt matches the instLTOfOrd semantics.
234	-- Decidable (a < b) then follows from DecidableEq Ordering (used by decide on ground terms).
235	instance instLTDimensionality : LT Dimensionality  := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
236	instance instLTRelational : LT Relational := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
237	instance instLTGrammar : LT Grammar := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
238	instance instLTChirality : LT Chirality := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
239	instance instLTProtection : LT Protection := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
240	instance instLTTopology : LT Topology := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
241	instance instLTPolarity : LT Polarity := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
242	instance instLTCriticality : LT Criticality := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩
243	instance instLTKineticChar : LT KineticChar := ⟨fun a b => compare a b = .lt⟩

248	-- ============================================================
249	-- CRYSTAL ARITHMETIC (§64, §68)
250	-- ============================================================
251	
252	-- The 17,280,000-type crystal: 3³ × 4⁵ × 5⁴
253	-- Exponent = count of primitives in each family (Arithmetic Ouroboros §68).
254	-- 𝓕₃: {F, G, S}         3 primitives × 3 values = 3³ = 27
255	-- 𝓕₄: {D, R, Γ, H, Ω}  5 primitives × 4 values = 4⁵ = 1,024
256	-- 𝓕₅: {T, P, Φ, K}     4 primitives × 5 values = 5⁴ = 625
257	-- Total: 27 × 1,024 × 625 = 17,280,000
258	
259	theorem crystal_F3_card : 3 ^ 3 = 27 := by decide
260	theorem crystal_F4_card : 4 ^ 5 = 1024 := by decide
261	theorem crystal_F5_card : 5 ^ 4 = 625 := by decide
262	theorem crystal_total : 27 * 1024 * 625 = 17280000 := by decide
263	
264	-- Arithmetic Ouroboros (§68): exponent of each base = count of primitives in that family.
265	-- This is not observed — it is forced by the product structure (§68.4).
266	theorem ouroboros_F3_exponent_equals_count : (3 : ℕ) = 3 := rfl  -- |𝓕₃| = 3
267	theorem ouroboros_F4_exponent_equals_count : (5 : ℕ) = 5 := rfl  -- |𝓕₄| = 5
268	theorem ouroboros_F5_exponent_equals_count : (4 : ℕ) = 4 := rfl  -- |𝓕₅| = 4
269	
270	-- Successor cycle 3 → 4 → 5 → 3 (§68): fixed-point-free, self-anchored.
271	theorem ouroboros_successor_cycle :
272	    (3 + 1 = 4) ∧ (4 + 1 = 5) ∧ (5 - 2 = 3) := by decide
273	
274	-- ============================================================
275	-- CROSS-PRIMITIVE AXIOMS
276	-- ============================================================
277	
278	-- Axiom C (revised): Holographic topology requires holographic dimensionality,
279	-- but the converse does not hold.
280	-- are (fully holographic, boundary encodes bulk) forces if' — no topology
281	-- of this kind is possible without the matching dimensionality split.
282	-- if' does NOT force are: imscriptive dimensionality permits oil
283	-- (structured lattice topology), as in the Stone and its co-types in the catalog
284	-- (imscription_grammar, true_agentic_agent, aleph_os, boundary operators, etc.).
285	-- The biconditional if' ↔ are was too strong; it only holds for the
286	-- maximally holographic case (AdS/CFT, quantum_gravity). The one-way implication
287	-- is the correct structural constraint.
288	-- (Revised 2026-05-03 after catalog evidence: 9 independently encoded O_inf systems
289	-- consistently carry if' + oil, never if' + are.)
290	-- Axiom C is now the predicate `ImscriptiveTopology` in Primitives/Imscription.lean.
291	-- As an axiom it read (d) (t) : t = are → d = if', with d untouched by the
292	-- hypothesis, so it asserted d = if' of EVERY dimensionality and proved False.
293	
294	-- Axiom B: Integer winding number requires persistent chirality.
295	-- oak requires H ≥ kick; ah requires H ≥ sure.
296	-- Axiom B is now the predicate `WindingNeedsChirality` in
297	-- Primitives/Imscription.lean. As an axiom it read (p) (h) : p ≥ ah → h ≥ sure,
298	-- with h untouched, so it asserted h ≥ sure of EVERY chirality — fee included,
299	-- which is false — and proved False.
300	
301	-- Axiom D: Holographic Closure — complete double-holomorphic encoding forces Frobenius.
302	-- Any system carrying if' (holographic dimensionality — boundary encodes bulk),
303	-- are (complete holographic topology — encoding is lossless), and ah or stronger
304	-- (integer winding — topological protection of the encoding) must have or' (μ∘δ=id).
305	--
306	-- Justification:
307	--   are  — the boundary encodes ALL bulk data; the encoding map δ is complete
308	--   if'  — the dimensionality split makes the boundary-bulk duality exact
309	--   ah — the winding number is conserved; the encoding cannot be unwound locally
310	-- Together: δ is complete (are), exact (if'), and topologically protected (ah).
311	-- A complete, exact, protected encoding map has a right inverse — this is or'.
312	--
313	-- Consequence: any imscription with d=if', t=are, p≥ah must have
314	-- pol=or'. Any other polarity assignment for such a system is structurally
315	-- inconsistent. In particular, the Hodge conjecture's correct imscription has
316	-- or' — the conventional yew assignment reflects open proof status,
317	-- not the true type. The grammar corrects this via Axiom D.
318	--
319	-- This is the grammar's original claim for the Hodge conjecture, the unique MPP
320	-- carrying both if' and are simultaneously among all seven problems.
321	-- Axiom D was here, as `holographic_closure_forces_frobenius`. It is now the
322	-- decidable predicate `ImscriptiveClosure` in Primitives/Imscription.lean,
323	-- because it constrains an imscription and Imscription is defined there. See
324	-- that file for why the axiom form was unsound.
325	
326	-- Tendency (not hard axiom): wool co-occurs with on.
327	-- An inexhaustible tower stands because its store is frozen.
328	-- Not an axiom because some wool systems (e.g. proto-languages) have egg.
329	-- Documented as tendency in §77 (consciousness navigator) and §75 (civilization).
330	
331	-- ============================================================
332	-- TIER STRUCTURE (§69 — Tier Gap Ladder)
333	-- ============================================================
334	
335	-- The ouroboricity tier is determined by (Φ, P, Ω, D) only.
336	-- R1: ⊙ + or' → O_inf  (overrides all Ω and D)
337	-- R2: Φ ∉ {⊙, 𐑮} → O₀
338	-- R3: ⊙ + 𐑷 → O₁  (P < or')
339	-- R4: ⊙ + Ω ≠ 0 + D ∈ {dead, if', ash} → O₂
340	-- R5: ⊙ + Ω ≠ 0 + array → O₂dag
341	-- R6: ⊙ + dead + mime + ah → O_inf_dag  (lateral: replicative opening, tested after R1)
342	-- Frobenius cliff: d(O₂dag, O_inf) ≈ 4.382 (non-tunable by gradient methods).
343	
344	/-- Ouroboricity tier as a decidable function of the four gate primitives. -/
345	inductive OuroboricityTier : Type where
346	  | O₀    -- non-critical
347	  | O₁    -- critical, no topological protection
348	  | O₂    -- critical, Ω-protected, D ≠ array
349	  | O₂dag -- critical, Ω-protected, D = array
350	  | O_inf  -- Special Frobenius (or' at ⊙) — terminal self-referential closure
351	  | O_inf_dag -- LATERAL to O_inf, not above it: self-replicative OPENING at ⊙.
352	              -- CLINK L8 reaches O_inf by closing terminally through or'. CLINK L9
353	              -- relinquishes or' and opens replicatively instead. That is a sideways
354	              -- move, and a linear order has no way to say "beside", so L9 fell through
355	              -- R1 into the O₂ default and read as a demotion. It is not a demotion and
356	              -- it is not an ascent: `dag` is how this codomain already writes a
357	              -- lateral (O₂ / O₂dag are siblings on one rung, split by dim), so the
358	              -- same idiom carries L9. There is deliberately NO tier above O_inf.
359	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord
360	
361	/-- Ouroboricity tier of the gate primitives.
362	
363	R6 (the dagger) keys on the REPLICATIVE OPENING triple — dim=dead ∧ top=mime ∧ prot=ah:
364	a point-like prime atom that crosses the moat and carries ℤ winding. Against L8's terminal
365	closure triple (dim=if' ∧ top=are ∧ prot=zoo: holographic state, holobound, non-Abelian
366	braid). Those two triples are what make the move lateral; they are not L9's whole tuple, so
367	the rule is not "L9 is O_inf_dag because it is L9".
368	
369	The triple names a real class in the catalog, not a bucket: ouroborus, self_replicating,
370	self_modeling, loop_space_s1, cycle_space, unit_circle_roots, iutt_closed_ring_4,
371	arithmetic_geometric_macrocycle, prime_chain_2_3, wheel_of_fortune, the_hanged_man — every
372	one replicative or cyclic. (A rule keyed instead on pol=out ∧ chir=wool swept 432 entries
373	including prions and Kerr black holes: two common coordinates, no class.)
374	
375	R1 STILL DOMINATES. 15 entries carry both or' and the replicative triple; they are
376	terminally closed AND replicative, and the Frobenius gate is the stronger claim, so the
377	dagger is tested only after R1 fails. This also keeps `r1_dominates`,
378	`o_inf_requires_phi_c` and `o_inf_requires_P_pm_sym` true: the dagger returns its own
379	constructor and never O_inf. -/
380	def ouroboricityTier (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
381	    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology) : OuroboricityTier :=
382	  match phi with
383	  | .woe | .haha | .err => .O₀
384	  | .monad | .roar =>
385	    if pol = .or' then .O_inf                    -- R1: Frobenius gate (terminal closure)
386	    else if dim = .dead ∧ top = .mime ∧ prot = .ah then
387	      .O_inf_dag                                 -- R6: lateral, replicative opening
388	    else match prot with
389	    | .awe => .O₁                                -- R3
390	    | _ => match dim with
391	      | .array => .O₂dag                           -- R5
392	      | _        => .O₂                              -- R4
393	
394	-- R1 is the dominant gate: or' at monad always gives O_inf.
395	theorem r1_dominates (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology) :
396	    ouroboricityTier .monad .or' prot dim top = .O_inf := by
397	  simp [ouroboricityTier]
398	
399	-- O_inf requires monad or roar: no other Phi value can give O_inf.
400	theorem o_inf_requires_phi_c (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
401	    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology)
402	    (h : ouroboricityTier phi pol prot dim top = .O_inf) :
403	    phi = .monad ∨ phi = .roar := by
404	  cases phi <;> simp [ouroboricityTier] at h <;> simp
405	
406	-- O_inf requires or': no other Polarity can give O_inf.
407	theorem o_inf_requires_P_pm_sym (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
408	    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology)
409	    (h : ouroboricityTier phi pol prot dim top = .O_inf) :
410	    pol = .or' := by
411	  cases phi <;> cases pol <;> cases prot <;> cases dim <;> cases top <;>
412	    simp [ouroboricityTier] at h <;> try rfl
413	
414	/-- The dagger is LATERAL, never O_inf: R1 owns or' and the dagger never returns O_inf. -/
415	theorem dag_is_not_O_inf (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
416	    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology)
417	    (h : ouroboricityTier phi pol prot dim top = .O_inf_dag) :
418	    pol ≠ .or' := by
419	  cases phi <;> cases pol <;> simp [ouroboricityTier] at h ⊢
420	
421	-- The Frobenius non-synthesizability statement (§23):
422	-- or' cannot be reached by the Polarity min (tensor bottleneck rule).
423	-- If either partner has P < or', the tensor product has P < or'.
424	def polarityTensor (a b : Polarity) : Polarity :=
425	  if compare a b = .lt then a else b   -- min rule: bottleneck primitive
426	
427	theorem frobenius_not_synthesizable (a b : Polarity)
428	    (ha : a ≠ .or') : polarityTensor a b ≠ .or' := by
429	  cases a with
430	  | church => cases b <;> decide
431	  | yew  => cases b <;> decide
432	  | out   => cases b <;> decide
433	  | nun  => cases b <;> decide
434	  | or' => contradiction
435	
436	-- ============================================================
437	-- DECIDABILITY INSTANCES (needed for proof automation)
438	-- ============================================================
439	
440	instance : DecidableEq Dimensionality  := inferInstance
441	instance : DecidableEq Topology        := inferInstance
442	instance : DecidableEq Relational      := inferInstance
443	instance : DecidableEq Polarity        := inferInstance
444	instance : DecidableEq Grammar         := inferInstance
445	instance : DecidableEq Fidelity        := inferInstance
446	instance : DecidableEq KineticChar     := inferInstance
447	instance : DecidableEq Granularity     := inferInstance
448	instance : DecidableEq Criticality     := inferInstance
449	instance : DecidableEq Protection      := inferInstance
450	instance : DecidableEq Stoichiometry   := inferInstance
451	instance : DecidableEq Chirality       := inferInstance
452	
453	end Imscribing.Primitives

-- Imscribing/Primitives/Core.lean
-- Canonical 12-primitive grammar (v0.5.69).
-- All names, value counts, and ordinal orderings match space_search/primitives.py.
-- Crystal: 3³ × 4⁵ × 5⁴ = 17,280,000 types.
--   𝓕₃ (3 values): F, G, S
--   𝓕₄ (4 values): D, R, Γ, H, Ω
--   𝓕₅ (5 values): T, P, Φ, K

import Mathlib.Order.Lattice
import Mathlib.Order.BoundedOrder.Basic

namespace Imscribing.Primitives

-- ============================================================
-- 𝓕₄ PRIMITIVES — 4 values each
-- ============================================================

-- 1. Dimensionality (D)  [𝓕₄]
-- Ordered: dead < ash < array < if'
-- if' = holographic (boundary encodes bulk); the monad symbol ⊙.
-- Replaces the non-canonical D_holo naming everywhere (v0.5.x).
inductive Dimensionality : Type where
  | dead     -- wedge/local: flat 2D sheet, no recursive nesting
  | ash  -- triangulated: simplicial / stratified, finite depth
  | array     -- infinite-dimensional: unbounded temporal/spatial generation
  | if'      -- imscriptive: the encoding writes what it encodes (⊙ = monad
             -- inside circle). Holographic — a boundary encoding a bulk it does
             -- not write — is the static subset of this, not a synonym for it.
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- 2. Relational Mode (R)  [𝓕₄]
-- Ordered: ado < tot < ear < ian
-- ado: hierarchical/supervisory; tot: compositional/categorical;
-- ear: bidirectional dagger (A ⊣ A†); ian: left-right / lateral.
inductive Relational : Type where
  | ado   -- supervisory / hierarchical: one-way authority
  | tot     -- categorical / compositional: functorial chaining
  | ear  -- dagger / reciprocal: A and A† co-define each other
  | ian      -- lateral / peer: symmetric two-way exchange
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- 3. Interaction Grammar (Γ)  [𝓕₄]
-- Ordered: vow < gag < measure < ooze
-- Categorical primitive (identity of composition rule required for non-⊥ meet).
inductive Grammar : Type where
  | vow    -- conjunctive / simultaneous: all conditions required
  | gag     -- disjunctive / alternative: any condition sufficient
  | measure    -- sequential / ordered: strict temporal or causal ordering
  | ooze  -- broadcast / universal: one-to-all coupling
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- 4. Chirality / chirality (H)  [𝓕₄]
-- Ordered: fee < kick < sure < wool
-- fee: no temporal memory; wool: topologically protected chirality.
-- Cross-primitive: wool tends to co-occur with on (frozen dynamics preserve
-- deep temporal structure), but this is a tendency, not a hard axiom.
inductive Chirality : Type where
  | fee      -- achiral: shift-invariant, no handedness to break
  | kick      -- soft chiral: period-2 under the shift
  | sure      -- persistent chiral: a descent through rank
  | wool   -- topological chiral, inexhaustible chirality
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- 5. Topological Protection (Ω)  [𝓕₄]
-- Ordered: awe < oak < ah < zoo
-- zoo: non-Abelian / non-standard protection (not necessarily stronger than ah
-- in a linear sense; occupies ordinal 4 as the maximally exotic tier).
inductive Protection : Type where
  | awe    -- no topological protection
  | oak   -- ℤ₂ symmetry protection
  | ah    -- integer winding number / ℤ protection
  | zoo   -- non-Abelian / non-standard protection
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- ============================================================
-- 𝓕₅ PRIMITIVES — 5 values each
-- ============================================================

-- 6. Topology (T)  [𝓕₅]
-- Ordered: judge < eat < mime < oil < are
-- are = holographic topology: non-local boundary-bulk correspondence.
-- are co-occurs with if' (see Axiom C below).
inductive Topology : Type where
  | judge  -- general graph: heterogeneous, locally connected
  | eat       -- inclusion / nested: hierarchical containment
  | mime   -- bowtie / figure-8: two-cycle closure, bifurcation point
  | oil      -- box / lattice: regular grid or torus
  | are     -- holographic: boundary fully encodes bulk (⊙)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- 7. Parity / Symmetry (P)  [𝓕₅]
-- Ordered: church < yew < out < nun < or'
-- or' is the Frobenius special condition (μ ∘ δ = id).
-- It is the tier singularity: overrides all Ω and D branching → O_inf.
-- or' cannot be synthesised by composition of P < or' partners (§23).
inductive Polarity : Type where
  | church    -- asymmetric: no symmetry axis
  | yew     -- phase symmetry: U(1) or continuous phase
  | out      -- ℤ₂ discrete symmetry (sign flip)
  | nun     -- full continuous symmetry (e.g. SO(n))
  | or'  -- Special Frobenius: μ ∘ δ = id; exact ℤ₂ at ⊙
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- 8. Criticality (Φ)  [𝓕₅]
-- Ordered: woe < monad < roar < err < haha
-- monad is absorbing under meet: meet(monad, x) = monad for all x.
-- This is not a standard linear meet — see note below.
inductive Criticality : Type where
  | woe        -- subcritical: stable, ordered phase
  | monad          -- real-axis Hermitian criticality: standard fixed point (absorbing)
  | roar  -- complex-axis criticality: analytic continuation required
                   -- (Lee-Yang edge, complex RG fixed point, ζ-function zeros)
                   -- Ordinal 2.33 in Python (non-integer; Lean uses rank 2)
  | err         -- exceptional-point criticality: non-Hermitian eigenvector coalescence
                   -- Square-root branch point; oak tendency
                   -- Ordinal 2.67 in Python (non-integer; Lean uses rank 3)
  | haha      -- supercritical: unstable, runaway
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

-- NOTE on monad absorbing meet:
-- The standard lattice meet (min) does not capture monad absorption.
-- In the grammar algebra: meet(monad, woe) = monad (not woe).
-- This requires a custom MeetSemilattice instance defined in Algebra.lean.
-- The Lean Ord derivation gives the ordinal ordering woe < monad < ...,
-- which is used for tier comparisons but not for the absorption rule.

-- 9. Kinetic Character (K)  [𝓕₅]
-- Ordered: yea < loll < egg < on < air
-- on: frozen by order (e.g. over-consolidated bureaucracy, catatonia).
-- air: frozen by disorder (many-body localization, dissociation, Soviet collapse).
-- Both on and air fail Gate 2 of the consciousness score (§VIII).
-- Restoration requires OPPOSITE interventions: on → disorder injection;

-- ============================================================
-- CROSS-PRIMITIVE AXIOMS
-- ============================================================

-- Axiom C (revised): Holographic topology requires holographic dimensionality,
-- but the converse does not hold.
-- are (fully holographic, boundary encodes bulk) forces if' — no topology
-- of this kind is possible without the matching dimensionality split.
-- if' does NOT force are: imscriptive dimensionality permits oil
-- (structured lattice topology), as in the Stone and its co-types in the catalog
-- (imscription_grammar, true_agentic_agent, aleph_os, boundary operators, etc.).
-- The biconditional if' ↔ are was too strong; it only holds for the
-- maximally holographic case (AdS/CFT, quantum_gravity). The one-way implication
-- is the correct structural constraint.
-- (Revised 2026-05-03 after catalog evidence: 9 independently encoded O_inf systems
-- consistently carry if' + oil, never if' + are.)
-- Axiom C is now the predicate `ImscriptiveTopology` in Primitives/Imscription.lean.
-- As an axiom it read (d) (t) : t = are → d = if', with d untouched by the
-- hypothesis, so it asserted d = if' of EVERY dimensionality and proved False.

-- Axiom B: Integer winding number requires persistent chirality.
-- oak requires H ≥ kick; ah requires H ≥ sure.
-- Axiom B is now the predicate `WindingNeedsChirality` in
-- Primitives/Imscription.lean. As an axiom it read (p) (h) : p ≥ ah → h ≥ sure,
-- with h untouched, so it asserted h ≥ sure of EVERY chirality — fee included,
-- which is false — and proved False.

-- Axiom D: Holographic Closure — complete double-holomorphic encoding forces Frobenius.
-- Any system carrying if' (holographic dimensionality — boundary encodes bulk),
-- are (complete holographic topology — encoding is lossless), and ah or stronger
-- (integer winding — topological protection of the encoding) must have or' (μ∘δ=id).
--
-- Justification:
--   are  — the boundary encodes ALL bulk data; the encoding map δ is complete
--   if'  — the dimensionality split makes the boundary-bulk duality exact
--   ah — the winding number is conserved; the encoding cannot be unwound locally
-- Together: δ is complete (are), exact (if'), and topologically protected (ah).
-- A complete, exact, protected encoding map has a right inverse — this is or'.
--
-- Consequence: any imscription with d=if', t=are, p≥ah must have
-- pol=or'. Any other polarity assignment for such a system is structurally
-- inconsistent. In particular, the Hodge conjecture's correct imscription has
-- or' — the conventional yew assignment reflects open proof status,
-- not the true type. The grammar corrects this via Axiom D.
--
-- This is the grammar's original claim for the Hodge conjecture, the unique MPP
-- carrying both if' and are simultaneously among all seven problems.
-- Axiom D was here, as `holographic_closure_forces_frobenius`. It is now the
-- decidable predicate `ImscriptiveClosure` in Primitives/Imscription.lean,
-- because it constrains an imscription and Imscription is defined there. See
-- that file for why the axiom form was unsound.

-- Tendency (not hard axiom): wool co-occurs with on.
-- An inexhaustible tower stands because its store is frozen.
-- Not an axiom because some wool systems (e.g. proto-languages) have egg.
-- Documented as tendency in §77 (consciousness navigator) and §75 (civilization).

-- ============================================================
-- TIER STRUCTURE (§69 — Tier Gap Ladder)
-- ============================================================

-- The ouroboricity tier is determined by (Φ, P, Ω, D) only.
-- R1: ⊙ + or' → O_inf  (overrides all Ω and D)
-- R2: Φ ∉ {⊙, 𐑮} → O₀
-- R3: ⊙ + 𐑷 → O₁  (P < or')
-- R4: ⊙ + Ω ≠ 0 + D ∈ {dead, if', ash} → O₂
-- R5: ⊙ + Ω ≠ 0 + array → O₂dag
-- R6: ⊙ + dead + mime + ah → O_inf_dag  (lateral: replicative opening, tested after R1)
-- Frobenius cliff: d(O₂dag, O_inf) ≈ 4.382 (non-tunable by gradient methods).

/-- Ouroboricity tier as a decidable function of the four gate primitives. -/
inductive OuroboricityTier : Type where
  | O₀    -- non-critical
  | O₁    -- critical, no topological protection
  | O₂    -- critical, Ω-protected, D ≠ array
  | O₂dag -- critical, Ω-protected, D = array
  | O_inf  -- Special Frobenius (or' at ⊙) — terminal self-referential closure
  | O_inf_dag -- LATERAL to O_inf, not above it: self-replicative OPENING at ⊙.
              -- CLINK L8 reaches O_inf by closing terminally through or'. CLINK L9
              -- relinquishes or' and opens replicatively instead. That is a sideways
              -- move, and a linear order has no way to say "beside", so L9 fell through
              -- R1 into the O₂ default and read as a demotion. It is not a demotion and
              -- it is not an ascent: `dag` is how this codomain already writes a
              -- lateral (O₂ / O₂dag are siblings on one rung, split by dim), so the
              -- same idiom carries L9. There is deliberately NO tier above O_inf.
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Ord

/-- Ouroboricity tier of the gate primitives.

R6 (the dagger) keys on the REPLICATIVE OPENING triple — dim=dead ∧ top=mime ∧ prot=ah:
a point-like prime atom that crosses the moat and carries ℤ winding. Against L8's terminal
closure triple (dim=if' ∧ top=are ∧ prot=zoo: holographic state, holobound, non-Abelian
braid). Those two triples are what make the move lateral; they are not L9's whole tuple, so
the rule is not "L9 is O_inf_dag because it is L9".

The triple names a real class in the catalog, not a bucket: ouroborus, self_replicating,
self_modeling, loop_space_s1, cycle_space, unit_circle_roots, iutt_closed_ring_4,
arithmetic_geometric_macrocycle, prime_chain_2_3, wheel_of_fortune, the_hanged_man — every
one replicative or cyclic. (A rule keyed instead on pol=out ∧ chir=wool swept 432 entries
including prions and Kerr black holes: two common coordinates, no class.)

R1 STILL DOMINATES. 15 entries carry both or' and the replicative triple; they are
terminally closed AND replicative, and the Frobenius gate is the stronger claim, so the
dagger is tested only after R1 fails. This also keeps `r1_dominates`,
`o_inf_requires_phi_c` and `o_inf_requires_P_pm_sym` true: the dagger returns its own
constructor and never O_inf. -/
def ouroboricityTier (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology) : OuroboricityTier :=
  match phi with
  | .woe | .haha | .err => .O₀
  | .monad | .roar =>
    if pol = .or' then .O_inf                    -- R1: Frobenius gate (terminal closure)
    else if dim = .dead ∧ top = .mime ∧ prot = .ah then
      .O_inf_dag                                 -- R6: lateral, replicative opening
    else match prot with
    | .awe => .O₁                                -- R3
    | _ => match dim with
      | .array => .O₂dag                           -- R5
      | _        => .O₂                              -- R4

-- R1 is the dominant gate: or' at monad always gives O_inf.
theorem r1_dominates (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology) :
    ouroboricityTier .monad .or' prot dim top = .O_inf := by
  simp [ouroboricityTier]

-- O_inf requires monad or roar: no other Phi value can give O_inf.
theorem o_inf_requires_phi_c (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology)
    (h : ouroboricityTier phi pol prot dim top = .O_inf) :
    phi = .monad ∨ phi = .roar := by
  cases phi <;> simp [ouroboricityTier] at h <;> simp

-- O_inf requires or': no other Polarity can give O_inf.
theorem o_inf_requires_P_pm_sym (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology)
    (h : ouroboricityTier phi pol prot dim top = .O_inf) :
    pol = .or' := by
  cases phi <;> cases pol <;> cases prot <;> cases dim <;> cases top <;>
    simp [ouroboricityTier] at h <;> try rfl

/-- The dagger is LATERAL, never O_inf: R1 owns or' and the dagger never returns O_inf. -/
theorem dag_is_not_O_inf (phi : Criticality) (pol : Polarity)
    (prot : Protection) (dim : Dimensionality) (top : Topology)
    (h : ouroboricityTier phi pol prot dim top = .O_inf_dag) :
    pol ≠ .or' := by
  cases phi <;> cases pol <;> simp [ouroboricityTier] at h ⊢

-- The Frobenius non-synthesizability statement (§23):
-- or' cannot be reached by the Polarity min (tensor bottleneck rule).
-- If either partner has P < or', the tensor product has P < or'.
def polarityTensor (a b : Polarity) : Polarity :=
  if compare a b = .lt then a else b   -- min rule: bottleneck primitive

theorem frobenius_not_synthesizable (a b : Polarity)
    (ha : a ≠ .or') : polarityTensor a b ≠ .or' := by
  cases a with
  | church => cases b <;> decide
  | yew  => cases b <;> decide
  | out   => cases b <;> decide
  | nun  => cases b <;> decide
  | or' => contradiction

-- ============================================================
-- DECIDABILITY INSTANCES (needed for proof automation)
-- ============================================================

instance : DecidableEq Dimensionality  := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Topology        := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Relational      := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Polarity        := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Grammar         := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Fidelity        := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq KineticChar     := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Granularity     := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Criticality     := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Protection      := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Stoichiometry   := inferInstance
instance : DecidableEq Chirality       := inferInstance

end Imscribing.Primitives

--   P3. Reflect (if', Axiom C*) : imscriptive self-protocol

-- Axiom C* (MillenniumAnkh one-way form): are → if' (not biconditional).
-- if' permits oil (e.g. odotOperator), unlike the imscribing_grammar biconditional.
--
-- The odotOperator is the paralogical unit. It holds dim = if' with top = oil
-- (NOT are), deliberately exercising the weaker Axiom C*: if' without are
-- is permissible. The O_inf Frobenius structure overrides the holographic
-- co-requirement. This is the formal signature of the paralogical.
--
-- ZFCt INTEGRATION: This file imports Primitives.ZFCt to connect the temporalized
-- ZFC framework to IG morphisms. The Imscriptions zfc, zfc_t, temporal_mathematics,
-- schrodinger_equation, heat_diffusion_equation, navier_stokes_equations,
-- wave_equation_temporal, and einstein_field_equations_dynamic are all usable as
-- IGProtocol arrow labels, endpoints, and tensor operands.

import Imscribing.CLINK
import Imscribing.Consciousness

open Primitives
open CLINK
open Consciousness
open Dimensionality Topology Relational Polarity Grammar
     Fidelity KineticChar Granularity Criticality Protection Stoichiometry Chirality

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- SECTION 1: IGProtocol
-- Inductive type indexed by Imscription × Imscription.
-- Each constructor corresponds to one element of the condensation notation.
-- Arrow labels are Imscriptions: the full 12-primitive annotation of transition
-- character. Any single dimension may be the salient one (the rest context).
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

inductive IGProtocol : Imscription → Imscription → Type where
  /-- Trivial self-transition (zero cost). -/
  | refl   : (s : Imscription) → IGProtocol s s
  /-- Labeled arrow: src —(label)→ tgt. -/
  | arrow  : (label src tgt : Imscription) → IGProtocol src tgt
  /-- Sequential composition: A→B then B→C  (the ɢ^ˌ chain). -/
  | seq    : IGProtocol a b → IGProtocol b c → IGProtocol a c
  /-- Parallel split: (A→B) and (A→C) give A → (B ⊗ C).
      The | operator lifts to tensorProduct on both targets. -/
  | prod   : IGProtocol a b → IGProtocol a c → IGProtocol a (tensorProduct b c)
  /-- Grammar annotation: ɢ^g[…] wrapper. -/
  | withGram : Grammar  → IGProtocol a b → IGProtocol a b
  /-- Memory annotation: […]_H wrapper. -/
  | withMem  : Chirality → IGProtocol a b → IGProtocol a b

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- SECTION 2: Structural measures
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- Arrow depth: total number of labeled transition steps. -/
def IGProtocol.depth : IGProtocol a b → ℕ
  | .refl _        => 0
  | .arrow _ _ _   => 1
  | .seq f g       => f.depth + g.depth
  | .prod f g      => max f.depth g.depth
  | .withGram _ p  => p.depth
  | .withMem _ p  => p.depth

/-- Dagger predicate: every arrow's label has rel = ear. -/
def IGProtocol.isDagger : IGProtocol a b → Bool
  | .refl _        => true
  | .arrow lbl _ _ => decide (lbl.rel = ear)
  | .seq f g       => f.isDagger && g.isDagger
  | .prod f g      => f.isDagger && g.isDagger
  | .withGram _ p  => p.isDagger
  | .withMem _ p  => p.isDagger

/-- Frobenius predicate: every arrow's label has pol = or'. -/
def IGProtocol.isFrobenius : IGProtocol a b → Bool
  | .refl _        => true
  | .arrow lbl _ _ => decide (lbl.pol = or')
  | .seq f g       => f.isFrobenius && g.isFrobenius
  | .prod f g      => f.isFrobenius && g.isFrobenius
  | .withGram _ p  => p.isFrobenius
  | .withMem _ p  => p.isFrobenius

-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- SECTION 3: LITANY AGAINST FEAR
-- Canonical IGProtocol encoding.
-- Reading: ɢ^ˌ[ 𐑣 —(𐑾)→ 𐑥 —(𐑦)→ { 𐑷 | 𐑯 } ]_𐑫
-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

private def litanyBase : Imscription := {
  dim  := dead,       top  := judge,       rel  := ado
  pol  := church,        fid  := age,            kin  := egg
  gran := bib,        gram := measure,         crit := woe
  chir := fee,            stoi := hung,           prot := awe }

/-- Cross: traversal state — pass over and through (mime crossing topology). -/
def litany_cross : Imscription := { litanyBase with top  := mime }
/-- Witness: imscriptive state — inner eye (if', satisfies Axiom C*: are forces if',
    here if' is present; are also set for the maximally holographic pairing). -/
def litany_witness : Imscription := { litanyBase with dim  := if', top := are }
/-- Nothing: the null state — where fear has gone (awe, woe). -/
def litany_nothing : Imscription := litanyBase
/-- Self: full-symmetry persistent state — only I will remain. -/
def litany_self : Imscription := { litanyBase with pol := nun, chir := wool }

-- Transition labels (dominant dimension annotates the arrow character):
private def lbl_face : Imscription := { litanyBase with rel := ian }
